html:
Antigua Guatemala was the capital of the Spanish Captaincy General of Guatemala, which ruled most of Central America, from 1543 until earthquakes destroyed much of it in 1773.

Founded after a mudslide buried the earlier capital, it lay in a valley below three volcanoes. It grew into a city of churches, convents, a university and the palaces of officials who governed from Chiapas to Costa Rica. Religious orders and Spanish families lived on the work of the Maya villages around it.

After the Santa Marta earthquakes of 1773, the crown moved the capital to a new site, today's Guatemala City. Antigua was left half in ruins, which kept its colonial streets intact. It became a World Heritage Site in 1979 and is the most visited town in Guatemala.
sum: Antigua Guatemala was the capital of the Spanish Captaincy General of Guatemala, which ruled most of Central America, from 1543 until earthquakes destroyed much of it in 1773.
